eva: Heads-up — saw tokenization / pre-tokenizer differences after HF->Redwood conversion. Small repro: the string 'Café — 50% ok' tokenizes differently and that cascaded into a small eval regression. Repro steps below.

sam: can you paste the converter output + config.json? most of these issues end up being either normalizer (NFKC vs NFC) or byte_fallback / add_prefix_space differences.

eva: sure, minimal repro (ran on my laptop):
```bash
# HF tokenizer (python)
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('some-open-llm')
print(t.tokenize("Café — 50% ok"))
# -> ['Caf', 'é', 'Ġ—', 'Ġ50', '%', 'Ġok']

# Redwood importer produced (after conversion):
# ['C', 'a', 'f', '\u00e9', ' ', '\u2014', ' ', '50', '%', ' ', 'ok']
```
This looks like the converter lost the ByteLevel pre-tokenizer and the normalizer settings (HF model used a byte fallback + add_prefix_space config).

maria: did that actually change any eval numbers? or just token lists?

eva: both. On our internal chit-chat LM eval, we saw a ~0.6 point hit in the pairwise quality metric for prompts containing non-ascii punctuation / diacritics. Also embeddings for short strings with emojis diverged (cosine down by ~0.02).

sam: ugh. two common failure modes: 1) converter ignores `normalizer` section (NFKC vs none) -> accent composition differences, 2) pre_tokenizer falls back to whitespace splitting instead of byte-level splitting. The config bits to check: `add_prefix_space`, `byte_fallback`, `normalizer` (type + args), `pre_tokenizer` (ByteLevel vs WhitespaceSplit), and `special_tokens_map`.

eva: here's the `tokenizer_config.json` snippet I got from the HF model: 
```json
{
  "add_prefix_space": true,
  "byte_fallback": true,
  "normalizer": {"type": "NFKC"},
  "pre_tokenizer": {"type": "ByteLevel"},
  "special_tokens": ["<bos>", "<eos>"]
}
```
Converter output had `byte_fallback: false` and `pre_tokenizer: WhitespaceSplit` for some reason.

sam: can you open an issue on the hf-importer repo and attach the minimal reproducer? i'll add a unit test that asserts round-trip tokenization equivalence for a small canonical corpus (accents, em-dash, ZWJ, emojis, percent signs, currency symbols). Also will add a config mapping check so `byte_fallback` can't silently flip off.

ci-bot: hf-importer/tests/tokenizer_compat.py failed on CI: test_byte_fallback_compat (see CI job 4823) :warning:

maria: we should also run the quantized model through the same tokenizer checks — quantization sometimes exposes subtle decode differences because of merged token boundaries. adding that to the regression suite could catch the BLEU/quality blips earlier.

sam: agreed. plan:
- sam: add importer unit tests + gating CI (tokenizer compatibility) by EOD tomorrow
- eva: collect a 200-sample corner-case corpus (accents, emojis, ligatures, ZWJ sequences, em/en dashes, percent/currency combos) and paste into the GH issue
- maria: re-run evals (baseline vs quantized) using both HF native tokenizer and converted tokenizer diff report; attach automated metric diff (BLEU/QA F1/embedding cosine)

eva: putting repro + corpus in https://github.com/redwood-inference/hf-importer/issues/57 now. cc @sam @maria :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. once tests are in we can fail the importer CI on any tokenization mismatch so this doesn't silently land and cause downstream regressions.

maria: also will add a note to onboarding playbook: "verify normalizer + pre_tokenizer parity when adding new HF models". small docs blurb saved us last time. :memo:

eva: nice. if anyone hits more weird splits, paste the raw token arrays (not detokenized text) — easy to miss a byte-level vs unicode-scalar split by eye.

sam: will follow up with PR link.

ci-bot: linked issue 57 to failing CI job 4823.

eva: thanks all — closing this thread once tests are green. :rocket:
